temperī (temporī)

adverb · Wiktionary

on time, at the right time

The adverb from tempus: “at the right or appointed time, in time” (Lewis & Short). Plautus’s and Cato’s word; it also serves for “in good time”.

Other words

  • ad tempus — at the appointed time

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.45.2: ad tempus redīre; Liv. 38.25 (ad tempus venīre, Lewis & Short); Traupman 366; Traupman 33

    Also “for the time being” (Cic. Off. 1.27), so the context must make the sense clear.

  • in tempore — at the right moment, just in time

    also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 364: in tempore ad eam vēnī

Examples

  • Numquid vīs? — Veniās temperī. — Memorem monēs.

    “Anything else?” — “Mind you come on time.” — “No need to remind me.”Plaut. Capt. 191

  • Vēnistī quidem temperī.

    Indeed, you’re on time.Traupman 83

  • Venī (venīte) temperī, quaesō.

    Be on time, please.Traupman 33

See also in good time, late.
